questions.prompt: A cafe offers \(3\) mains and \(4\) drinks. How many meal-and-drink choices are possible?
questions.answer: Use the multiplication principle: each main can be paired with each drink, giving \(3\times4=12\) choices.

questions.prompt: A code has one letter followed by one digit. How many codes are possible using \(26\) letters and \(10\) digits?
questions.answer: There are \(26\) choices for the letter and \(10\) for the digit, so \(26\times10=260\) codes are possible.

questions.prompt: How many ways can \(5\) students be arranged in a line?
questions.answer: There are \(5\) choices for the first position, then \(4\), then \(3\), \(2\), and \(1\). Thus the number is \(5!=120\).

questions.prompt: From \(8\) runners, how many ordered gold-silver-bronze results are possible?
questions.answer: Order matters. There are \(8\) choices for gold, \(7\) for silver, and \(6\) for bronze, giving \(8\times7\times6=336\).

questions.prompt: How many \(3\)-person committees can be chosen from \(10\) people?
questions.answer: Order does not matter, so use combinations: \[\binom{10}{3}=\frac{10\times9\times8}{3\times2\times1}=120.\]

questions.prompt: A password has \(2\) different letters followed by \(2\) digits, where digits may repeat. How many passwords are possible?
questions.answer: The letters have \(26\times25\) choices because they are different. The digits have \(10\times10\) choices. Total: \(26\times25\times10^2=65000\).

questions.prompt: How many subsets of size \(4\) can be chosen from a set of \(12\) objects?
questions.answer: A subset is unordered, so \[\binom{12}{4}=495.\]

questions.prompt: How many distinct arrangements are there of the letters in LEVEL?
questions.answer: There are \(5\) letters with two Ls and two Es repeated. The count is \[\frac{5!}{2!2!}=30.\]

questions.prompt: A route from A to C goes through B. There are \(4\) routes from A to B and \(6\) routes from B to C. How many A-to-C routes are possible?
questions.answer: Choose one route for each leg. By the multiplication principle, the total is \(4\times6=24\).

questions.prompt: A quiz has \(6\) true-false questions. How many answer strings are possible?
questions.answer: Each question has \(2\) possible answers, so the total is \(2^6=64\).

questions.prompt: How many ways can \(4\) books be selected from \(9\) and then arranged on a shelf?
questions.answer: This is an ordered selection of \(4\) from \(9\): \[{}^9P_4=9\times8\times7\times6=3024.\]

questions.prompt: A hand of \(5\) cards is drawn from a \(52\)-card deck. How many possible hands are there?
questions.answer: A hand is unordered, so the number is \[\binom{52}{5}=2598960.\]

questions.prompt: How many \(4\)-digit numbers can be formed from digits \(0\) to \(9\) if repetition is allowed and the first digit cannot be \(0\)?
questions.answer: The first digit has \(9\) choices. Each remaining digit has \(10\) choices. Hence \(9\times10^3=9000\).

questions.prompt: How many \(4\)-digit numbers can be formed from digits \(0\) to \(9\) if no digit repeats and the first digit cannot be \(0\)?
questions.answer: Choose the first digit in \(9\) ways, then the remaining digits in \(9\), \(8\), and \(7\) ways. Total: \(9\times9\times8\times7=4536\).

questions.prompt: A team needs \(2\) physicists from \(5\) and \(3\) mathematicians from \(7\). How many teams are possible?
questions.answer: Choose independently from each group: \[\binom{5}{2}\binom{7}{3}=10\times35=350.\]

questions.prompt: How many ways can \(8\) people be seated around a circular table, counting rotations as the same?
questions.answer: For circular arrangements, fix one person and arrange the other \(7\). This gives \((8-1)!=7!=5040\).

questions.prompt: A box contains \(6\) red and \(5\) blue balls. How many unordered selections of \(4\) balls contain exactly \(2\) red and \(2\) blue?
questions.answer: Choose \(2\) of the \(6\) red and \(2\) of the \(5\) blue: \[\binom{6}{2}\binom{5}{2}=15\times10=150.\]

questions.prompt: How many paths from \((0,0)\) to \((4,3)\) use only right and up steps?
questions.answer: Every path has \(4\) right steps and \(3\) up steps, \(7\) steps total. Choose positions for the \(3\) up steps: \[\binom{7}{3}=35.\]

questions.prompt: A licence plate has \(3\) letters followed by \(3\) digits. Letters may repeat, but the digits must be all different. How many plates are possible?
questions.answer: The letters give \(26^3\) possibilities. The digits give \(10\times9\times8\). Total: \[26^3\times10\times9\times8=12654720.\]

questions.prompt: A committee of \(5\) is chosen from \(6\) engineers and \(5\) physicists. How many committees contain at least \(3\) engineers?
questions.answer: Split into cases: \(3\), \(4\), or \(5\) engineers. The count is \[\binom{6}{3}\binom{5}{2}+\binom{6}{4}\binom{5}{1}+\binom{6}{5}\binom{5}{0}=20\cdot10+15\cdot5+6=281.\]
